# Anikit — full reference for LLMs

Contents: 1. Agent playbook · 2. Recipes · 3. API reference

---

# AGENTS.md — using Anikit in an app

A compact playbook for coding agents (and humans) writing animations with `anikit`. Every `ts` block below type-checks against the real API. More: `llms-full.txt` (this file + task recipes + the full reference, in one file; `docs/recipes.md` and `docs/api.md` in the repo).

## Install & import

```ts
import { animate, timeline, stagger, spring, scrollTrigger, effects, testing } from 'anikit';
// 'anikit/lean' streams anikit.wasm instead of embedding it (smaller JS): `await init()` before synchronous helpers.
```

Calls work immediately: the WebAssembly core loads in the background and queues `animate()`/`timeline()` work until it's ready. Helpers that return a value at once (`ease()`, `morph()`, `pathLength()`, `staggerValues()`, `world()`) need it loaded, so `await ready` first in code that runs at startup.

## Quick start: a polished page in five lines

```ts
import { recipe } from 'anikit';
recipe('hero-reveal', '.hero');                              // masked headline rise + subtitle fade
recipe('magnetic-buttons', '.hero');                         // buttons lean towards the cursor
recipe('scroll-story', 'main', { children: 'section' });     // sections rise in on scroll
recipe('parallax-gallery', '.gallery');                      // images drift at different depths
```

Or start from a working project: `npx anikit new vanilla my-site` (no build step), `npx anikit new vite my-site`, or `npx anikit new react my-site`. `recipeNames()` lists every recipe (`hero-reveal`, `scroll-story`, `magnetic-buttons`, `text-scramble`, `parallax-gallery`, `stagger-in`, `draw-svg`, `count-up`, `tilt-cards`); each returns a handle with `revert()`. Every option of every API is in `docs/api.schema.json` (JSON Schema). Unknown options and recipe names produce an `anikit:` warning or error with a "did you mean" and a `docs/api.md#…` link.

In React, `import { useRecipe, useAnimate, useAnikit, useSpring, useScroll, Presence } from 'anikit/react'`: everything a hook creates is reverted on unmount. Vue: `v-recipe` / `v-anikit` directives from `anikit/vue`; Svelte: `use:recipe` / `use:anikit` actions from `anikit/svelte`.

## Want X → use Y

| Want | Use |
|---|---|
| Animate elements (enter, exit, state change) | `animate(targets, { x, opacity, … }, { duration, ease, delay })` |
| One after another / overlapping steps | `timeline().add(…).add(…, '-=0.2')`, or `sequence([...])` |
| Offset many elements | `delay: stagger(0.05, { from: 'center', grid: [cols, rows] })` |
| Natural, interruptible motion (pointer, toggles) | `spring(el, { x, y }, { stiffness, damping })` (retargets keep velocity) |
| One value driving many properties (progress, drag, slider) | `const p = motionValue(0); bindValues(el, { x: p.map([0, 1], [0, 300]), opacity: p }); p.spring(0.5)` |
| Endless logo / ticker row | `marquee('.logos', { speed: 60, pauseOnHover: true, scrollBoost: 0.5 })` |
| Buttons that lean towards the cursor; layered parallax | `magnetic('.cta', { strength: 0.35 })`; `parallax('.bg', { speed: -0.4 })` |
| A timed spring inside a timeline | `ease: 'spring(bounce: 0.3, duration: 0.6)'` |
| Throw / glide with momentum | `inertia(el, { x: { velocity, min, max, snap } })` or `draggable(el, { inertia: true })` |
| Play when visible | `inView(sel, (el) => { … }, { once: true })`, or `scrollTriggerBatch(sel, { animation: (el) => animate(…, { autoplay: false }) })` |
| Scrub / pin with scrolling | `scrollTrigger({ trigger, start, end, scrub, pin, animation: timeline({ autoplay: false }) })` |
| Progress bar / parallax | `scroll(animate(el, …, { ease: 'linear', autoplay: false }), { target, offset })` |
| Animate a layout change | `flip(targets, () => changeLayout())` |
| Text by characters / words / lines | `splitText(el, { type: 'words,chars' })` then animate `.chars` |
| Typewriter, scramble, counters | `{ text: 'Hi' }`, `{ text: { value, type: 'scramble' } }`, `{ textContent: 1200 }` + `format` |
| SVG shape morph / line draw / follow a path | `{ d: otherPath }`, `{ draw: [0, 1] }`, `{ path: { path: '#track', rotate: true } }` |
| Ready-made entrances / attention seekers | `effects.fadeIn(el)`, `effects.shake(el)`, `effects.countUp(el, { to })` (39 presets) |
| Hover / press feedback | `hover(el, (el) => { …; return () => … })`, `press(…)` |
| Drag, swipe, carousels | `draggable(el, { type: 'x', bounds, inertia: true, snap })`; `observer({ onUp, onDown })` for swipes/wheel |
| Physics: falling, colliding, throwable things | `world({ container })`, `.bind(els)`, `.dragging()` |
| Thousands of things on a canvas | `batch(n, props)` (one Float32Array) or `world().addMany()` |
| Real-time 3D scene (WebGL2): PBR objects, shadows, bloom, clicks | `scene(canvas, { environment, shadows, bloom })`, `s.add(sphere(), { material: 'chrome' })`, `animate(obj.position, …)` (also `anikit/scene`) |
| 3D points / tilt / transform strings | `scene3d()`, `tilt(el)`, `{ transform: 'rotateY(180deg)' }` |
| 100k particles | `pointCloud()` + `glow()` |
| Photoreal 3D captures, splat morphs, 100k–1M soft 3D points on the GPU | `import { splats } from 'anikit/splats'`; `splats(canvas, set)` with `splats.load('x.ply')` or procedural `splats.fromText/fromSDF/fromMesh/fromPoints`; animate `layer.fx`, `layer.camera`, `layer.transform`, or `layer.morph(other)` |
| Off-main-thread transform/opacity | `compositor(el, props, options)` |
| A polished pattern in one call | `recipe('hero-reveal' \| 'scroll-story' \| 'magnetic-buttons' \| 'text-scramble' \| …, el, options)` |
| React | `anikit/react`: `useAnikit(() => { … })` (scoped, reverted on unmount), `useAnimate()`, `useRecipe()`, `useSpring()`, `useScroll()`, `<Presence>` |
| Cleanup in React/Vue/Svelte | `const ctx = context(() => { … }, rootEl); return () => ctx.revert()` |
| Respect "reduce motion" | `engine.reducedMotion = 'user'` once at startup |
| Shader effect on real DOM (ripple, shatter, dissolve, curl, pixelate, wave, glass) | `htmlEffect('#card', 'shatter', { duration: 1.2 })`; `'out'` effects leave it hidden until `revert()`, or use `mode: 'in'` to reveal |
| Live HTML on a 3D mesh (card, screen, cube face) with working clicks | `s.add(plane(1.6, 1), { rotation: [Math.PI / 2, 0, 0], material: { color: '#000', emissive: '#fff', map: htmlTexture('#panel') } })`; keep `#panel` rendered off-screen, not `display: none` |
| Live DOM as a WebGL texture / canvas | `const hc = htmlCanvas('#card', { target: gl }); await hc.ready; gl.bindTexture(gl.TEXTURE_2D, hc.texture)` (native HTML-in-Canvas when the element is a child of `<canvas layoutsubtree>` and the browser has it; SVG foreignObject fallback elsewhere) |
| GIF / WebM / PNG of a page | `record(el, { duration, fps })`, `screenshot(el)`, CLI `npx anikit-record` |
| A video file (MP4) rendered in Node | `npx anikit-render --init film.mjs` (see Making videos below) |
| Verify headlessly | `testing.useFakeTime()`, `testing.advance(s)`, `engine.inspect()`, `testing.captureWarnings()` |

## Rules of thumb

- **Times are in seconds**: `duration: 0.6`, `delay: 0.1`, `stagger(0.05)`, `seek(1.2)`. Only the raw clock is in ms: `engine.tick(ms)`, `engine.time`, `engine.onFrame((timeMs, dtMs) => …)`.
- **Properties:**
  - **Transforms:** `x`, `y`, `z`, `rotate`, `rotateX`/`Y`, `scale`, `scaleX`/`Y`, `skew`, `xPercent`/`yPercent`, `perspective`. Composed per element and written once per frame; use them for motion instead of `left`/`top`. Numbers are px / deg / unitless.
  - **Everything else:** any CSS property in camelCase (`backgroundColor`), CSS variables (`'--hue'`), `attr: {…}`, plain-object keys, `textContent` counters, `text` typewriter/scramble, `d` morphing, `path` motion paths, `draw` stroke drawing, and `transform` (whole transform strings).
- **Values:** a single value means "from current to this"; `[from, to]` or `[a, b, c]` are keyframes (`null` = current); `'+=50'` is relative; `(el, i, count) => v` and `'random(0, 100)'` run per target (a function may also return keyframes: `(el, i) => [0, i * 10]`).
- **Options** go in the third argument (`{ duration, ease, delay, repeat, yoyo, autoplay, onComplete }`) or among the properties. GSAP-style `stagger: 0.05` and `loop: true` work too. Unknown keys warn with a suggestion (other libraries' names such as `easing`, `iterations`, `fill` are mapped to the anikit ones).
- **Easing:** CSS (`'ease-out'`, `'cubic-bezier(…)'`, `'steps(4)'`), Penner (`'outCubic'`), GSAP (`'power2.inOut'`, `'back.out(1.7)'`), springs (`'spring(bounce: 0.3, duration: 0.6)'` or `{ stiffness, damping }`), `'custom(M0,0 C…)'`, or a function. Default `'outQuad'`, duration `0.5`.
- **Overwrite:** a new animation on the same property takes it over (`overwrite: false` to opt out), so re-triggering is safe.
- **Controllers** (`animate`, `timeline`, `batch`): `play pause reverse restart seek(s) complete cancel kill revert`, `progress`, `time`, `speed`; `await` them for completion.
- **Cleanup:** `anim.revert()` restores the original inline styles; in components wrap setup in `context(fn, rootEl)` and call `ctx.revert()` on unmount; `matchMedia().add(query, fn)` for responsive setups.
- **Performance:** hundreds of DOM elements are fine with `animate()`; thousands of canvas things → `batch()`/`world()`; many 3D points → `scene3d()`; 100k particles → `pointCloud()` + `glow({ budget })`; a busy main thread → `compositor()`. `engine.speed` scales everything (slow motion).

## Snippets

```ts
import { animate, timeline, stagger, scrollTrigger, scrollTriggerBatch, spring, effects } from 'anikit';

// Entrance with stagger
animate('.card', { y: [24, 0], opacity: [0, 1] }, { duration: 0.6, ease: 'outCubic', delay: stagger(0.06) });

// Sequenced timeline with overlap and labels (position after the props or after the options)
timeline({ defaults: { ease: 'outCubic', duration: 0.5 } })
  .add('.title', { y: [30, 0], opacity: [0, 1] })
  .add('.sub', { opacity: [0, 1] }, '-=0.3')
  .label('cta')
  .add('.cta', { scale: [0.8, 1] }, { ease: 'spring(bounce: 0.4)' }, 'cta');

// Scroll-scrubbed, pinned section (the animation is created paused)
scrollTrigger({ trigger: '.story', start: 'top top', end: '+=1200', pin: true, scrub: 0.4,
  animation: timeline({ autoplay: false }).add('.story .a', { x: [0, 400] }).add('.story .b', { opacity: [0, 1] }) });

// Reveal on scroll: play on enter, reverse when scrolling back above
scrollTriggerBatch('.reveal', { start: 'top 85%', toggleActions: 'play none none reverse',
  animation: (el) => animate(el, { y: [40, 0], opacity: [0, 1] }, { autoplay: false }) });

// Pointer-following with momentum
addEventListener('pointermove', (e) => spring('.dot', { x: e.clientX, y: e.clientY }, { stiffness: 300, damping: 25 }));

// Presets
effects.fadeIn('.toast');
effects.shake('#password');
effects.countUp('#revenue', { to: 128400, format: { style: 'currency', currency: 'USD' } });
```

```ts
import { world, batch, scene3d, engine, pointCloud, textPoints, glow, record, scene, plane, sphere, box, animate } from 'anikit';

// Physics: DOM elements that fall, collide and can be thrown
const w = world({ container: '#stage', restitution: 0.4 });
w.bind('#stage .ball', { rotate: true });
w.dragging();
w.pointer({ mode: 'repel' });

// Real-time WebGL2 scene: PBR, shadows, bloom; objects animate like any target
const s3 = scene('#gl', { camera: { position: [0, 2, 6] }, environment: 'studio', shadows: true, bloom: true });
s3.add(plane(20, 20), { material: { color: '#333', roughness: 0.9 } });
const orb = s3.add(sphere(0.6, 64), { material: 'gold', position: [0, 0.6, 0] });
orb.on('click', () => animate(orb.position, { y: [0.6, 1.6, 0.6] }, { duration: 0.8 }));
s3.instances(box(0.1, 0.1, 0.1), 5000, (i, o) => o.position.set((i % 70) - 35, 0, (i / 70 | 0) - 35));
s3.orbit({ autoRotate: 8 });

// 3D point cloud on a canvas
const cloud = batch(20000, { x: (i) => [0, Math.cos(i) * 300], y: (i) => [0, Math.sin(i * 1.3) * 300], z: (i) => [0, Math.sin(i) * 300] }, { duration: 2 });
const view3d = scene3d({ canvas: '#c' }).orbit({ autoRotate: 10 });
engine.onFrame(() => view3d.draw(cloud, { size: 1.5, color: '#9cf' }));

// 100k glowing particles that morph between shapes (text → sphere) and part around the pointer
const pc = pointCloud(100_000, { shapes: [textPoints('hello', 100_000, { width: 700 }), (i, n) => {
  const y = 1 - (2 * i) / n, r = Math.sqrt(1 - y * y), t = i * 2.4; return [Math.cos(t) * r * 250, y * 250, Math.sin(t) * r * 250];
}] });
const g = glow('#bg', { trail: 0.5, background: '#07080b' });
const cam = scene3d({ fov: 40, camera: { z: 1000 } });
g.resize(innerWidth, innerHeight);
let ptr: { x: number; y: number } | undefined;
addEventListener('pointermove', (e) => (ptr = { x: e.clientX, y: e.clientY }));
engine.onFrame(() => g.render(cam, pc, { size: 1.2, intensity: 0.3, lens: ptr }));
pc.morph(1, { duration: 2.5, ease: 'inOutCubic' });   // or: pc.morph(1); pc.mix = scrollProgress;

// Record any of the above to a GIF, frame-exact
const rec = await record('#stage', { duration: 2, fps: 30 });
rec.download('stage.gif');
```

```ts
import { animate, flip, presence, exit, viewTransition, scroll, compositor, splitText, stagger, gesture, engine } from 'anikit';
declare const item: HTMLElement, panel: HTMLElement, open: boolean, thumb: HTMLElement, hero: HTMLElement;
declare function applyFilter(): void;
declare function showDetail(): void;
declare function detailImg(): HTMLElement | null;

// Layout and presence: list changes animate; removed items fade out in place, then go
flip('.card', () => applyFilter(), { fade: true });
const todos = presence('#todos', { enter: { opacity: [0, 1], y: [-8, 0] }, exit: { opacity: 0 } });
todos.add(item); todos.remove(item);
exit('.toast');                                            // animate out, then remove
animate(panel, { height: open ? 'auto' : 0 });             // accordions

// Shared element (thumbnail -> detail) with the View Transitions API, FLIP fallback
viewTransition(() => showDetail(), { ease: 'spring(bounce: 0.2, duration: 0.5)', names: { hero: [thumb, () => detailImg()] } });

// Scroll-linked on the compositor (native ScrollTimeline where available)
scroll(compositor('.hero', { scale: [1, 1.2], opacity: [1, 0] }, { ease: 'linear' }), { target: hero, offset: ['start start', 'end start'] });

// Text lines rising from behind a mask, re-split on resize
splitText('.lede', { type: 'lines', mask: 'lines', autoSplit: true, onSplit: ({ lines }) => animate(lines, { yPercent: [100, 0] }, { delay: stagger(0.08) }) });

// Pinch-zoom / rotate / pan with limits and momentum
gesture('#photo', { minScale: 1, maxScale: 5 });

// Follow an SVG path exactly as drawn (viewBox and page position mapped)
animate('.dot', { path: { path: '#route', align: true, rotate: true } }, { duration: 4 });

// Reduced motion that keeps fades and colour changes
engine.reducedMotion = 'user';
engine.reducedMotionMode = 'fade';
```

Accessibility: with `engine.reducedMotion = 'user'`, add `engine.reducedMotionMode = 'fade'` to keep fades and colour changes while movement (transforms, paths, layout) jumps to its end.

Task-sized versions (hero, list, carousel, page transition, counters, FLIP, React cleanup, recording, Node video, Python) are in the recipes section of `llms-full.txt`.

## Verifying your work

```ts
import { animate, testing, engine } from 'anikit';

await testing.ready;
testing.useFakeTime();                        // deterministic: no requestAnimationFrame
const warnings = testing.captureWarnings();   // BEFORE the code under test
const el = document.createElement('div');
document.body.append(el);
animate(el, { x: 100 }, { duration: 1, ease: 'linear' });
testing.advance(0.5);                         // el.style.transform === 'translate(50px,0px)'
engine.inspect();                             // [{ type: 'tween', target: 'div', props: ['x'], progress: 0.5, … }]
testing.finishAll();                          // run until idle
console.assert(warnings.length === 0, warnings.join('\n'));
testing.reset();                              // between tests
```

In a headless browser, `window.__ANIKIT__` is the engine (`.manual(true)`, `.tick(ms)`, `.inspect()`). Scroll triggers, pinning and dragging need layout: check them in Chromium (Playwright), not happy-dom/jsdom.

## Common mistakes

Most of these print an `anikit:` warning that names the fix; read the console.

| Symptom / warning | Cause → fix |
|---|---|
| Nothing moves; "selector … matched no elements" | Typo, missing `.`/`#` (the warning suggests one), or the script ran before the DOM: run after `DOMContentLoaded` or from a module script. In tests: call `testing.advance()`; nothing moves in fake time otherwise. |
| "received null as its target" | A `querySelector()`/ref returned null. Check the element exists when the code runs. |
| Animation takes minutes; "duration is 600 seconds" | Times are seconds: `duration: 0.6`, `stagger(0.05)`. |
| "unknown animation option" / "unknown option" | Misspelled option (the warning suggests the right one) or an option the API doesn't have, e.g. `spring()` has no `delay`/`ease`. |
| "is not a CSS property" | Misspelled property (`colour` → `color`), or an option put among the properties. |
| "unknown easing" (throws) | Use a listed name (`'outCubic'`, `'power2.out'`, `'ease-in-out'`); the error suggests the nearest. |
| "rotate is an angle" / "opacity goes from 0 to 1" | Wrong unit: `rotate: 45` or `'0.5turn'`; `opacity: 0.5`, not `50`. |
| Element jumps at the start | Give an explicit start value: `x: [0, 100]`, `opacity: [0, 1]`. |
| `left`/`top` don't move it; "has no effect … position: static" | Animate `x`/`y` (transforms, also faster), or give the element `position: relative`. |
| Timeline children start from the wrong value | Sequential tweens of a property chain automatically; for parallel ones give `[from, to]`. |
| Scroll animation runs on load or flashes | Create it with `autoplay: false` and pass it as `animation` (the trigger pauses it, but `autoplay: false` avoids a first frame). |
| `scrollTrigger({ animation: (el) => … })` throws | That form belongs to `scrollTriggerBatch()`; `scrollTrigger` takes one animation. |
| Pinned section has the wrong height after images load | Call `refreshScrollTriggers()` after layout changes. |
| Styles remain after unmount / route change | Use `context()` and `ctx.revert()`. |
| `ease()`/`morph()` throw "core is still loading" | `await ready` (or `await init()` with `anikit/lean`) before synchronous helpers. |
| `onFrame` motion is 1000× too fast | `onFrame` gives `(timeMs, dtMs)`: divide by 1000 for seconds. |
| `draggable(el).x` is undefined | `draggable()` returns an array: `const [drag] = draggable(el)`. |
| Python: `stagger(5)` gives a list; a timeline step lands at the wrong time | In Python an int first argument is a count (`stagger(5, 0.1)`); for a delay pass seconds (`delay=stagger(0.05, from_="center")`). `tl.add(target, props, "-=0.2", duration=0.5)`: the position is the third argument, options are keywords. |

## Making videos (compositions)

Use this when asked for a video, trailer, title sequence, product film or animated clip. Output is frame-exact MP4/WebM; nothing depends on machine speed.

```bash
npx anikit-render --doctor                           # first time: checks Node, @napi-rs/canvas, ffmpeg and the build, with fixes
npx anikit-render --init film.mjs                    # a working starter: 3D cubes + particles + type + impact + grade
npx anikit-render --init fly.mjs --template journey  # a 3D fly-through: neon city, chrome gates, shattering knot, 3D wordmark
npx anikit-render film.mjs --preview 15 --out pv/    # every 15th frame as JPEG, fast; look at these before rendering
npx anikit-render film.mjs --out film.mp4 --workers 4 [--audio track.wav] [--fade-out 0.5]
```

The module default-exports `async ({ anikit, node }) => composition`. Building blocks, all rendered in WebAssembly:

| Want | Use |
|---|---|
| Scenes, timing | `composition({ width, height, fps, duration, motionBlur, post })`, `.scene(name, start, end, { enter, step, draw, transition, timeScale, motionBlur })`, `.cue(t, fn)` |
| Punch | `.impact(t, { shake, flash, flashOpacity, aberration, decay, shockwave, origin })` — applied to the finished frame; `shockwave` sends a refracting ring out from `origin` |
| Film look | `post: { aa, bloom, bloomThreshold, bloomRadius, streaks, streakLength, rays, raysCenter, flares, aberration, vignette, grain, zoomBlur, exposure, contrast, saturation, shadows, highlights }` — any value can be `(t) => …` |
| Slow motion / bullet time | scene `timeScale: (local) => 0.1…1` — slows tweens, particles, physics together; choreograph on `draw({ clock })` (the slowed scene clock) and place hits with `film.impact(film.timeAt('scene', clockSeconds), …)` |
| Solid 3D | `renderer3d({ width, height })`, `mesh.cube() / sphere() / torus() / torusKnot() / plane() / cylinder() / heightfield() / text() / custom()`, `instances(n, i => ({ x, y, z, rx, ry, rz, scale, sx, sy, sz, color }))`, `render(scene3d, [{ mesh, instances, material, cull, blend }], { background, fog, sky, horizon, ground, strips })` |
| Materials that don't look plain | dark bodies + light: `{ metal: 0.9, iridescence: 0.3 }` chrome, `{ lines: 1.5, lineColor, grid: [1, 1] }` glowing edges, `{ pulse: 2, pulsePhase: t }` travelling light, `{ emissive: 1 }` neon; set `strips` for crisp chrome highlights |
| Flying camera ("journey") | `flightPath(points, { lookAhead, bank })`, `path.timing([[sec, frac], …])`, `path.apply(cam, s(t), extraRoll, { shake })` (handheld wobble); `cam.roll` for barrel rolls (unwind the shortest way: wrap to ±180° first); `render(…, { motionBlur: true })` with composition `motionBlur: 1` for ghost-free speed |
| Stars, dust, sparks in 3D | `{ points, colors, size, intensity, streak, fog }` items in `render()` — depth-tested, streak with camera motion; accepts an `emitter()` |
| Explosions | `shatter(mesh, { force, spin, gravity })` → `{ mesh, instances }`; `shards.update(t - hitTime)` |
| Particles as light or ink | `pointCloud(n, { shapes })` + `glow(node.glowTarget(w, h), { mode: 'light' | 'ink' })` |
| Sparks | `emitter({ rate, life, speed, spread, gravity, colors })`, `.burst(n)` |
| Physics | `world({ bounds, gravity })` |
| Type | `typeFx(ctx, text, x, y, { t, start, effect: 'slam' | 'rise' | 'wave' | 'type' | 'scramble' | 'fade' })`; `textPoints(text, n)` for type made of particles |
| Transitions between scenes | `transition: { duration, type: 'whip' | 'push' | 'iris' | 'slice' | 'zoom' | 'flash' | 'mask' | fn }` |
| Music sync | `analyzeAudio(samples, rate)` → `bpm`, `beats`, `onsets`, `at(t)` |

**Rules that keep films correct**
1. Start tweens and simulations in `enter()`; advance simulations in `step(f)` with **`f.dt`** (engine seconds, already scaled by `timeScale`). `draw()` only reads state — with motion blur it runs several times per frame.
2. Don't read wall-clock time. `Math.random` is seeded by `anikit-render`, so parallel workers produce identical frames.
3. Solid 3D: draw the renderer's pixels first (`ctx.putImageData(new ImageData(px, w, h), 0, 0)`), then 2D particles (`glow`) with `globalCompositeOperation = 'lighter'`, then type. Prefer `points` items inside `render()` for particles that must hide behind geometry.
6. Plain flat-coloured shapes look cheap. Use near-black bodies and put the colour in light: chrome + `strips`, glowing `lines`, `pulse`, `emissive`, bloom. Two or three hues per shot.
4. One shared `scene3d` per shot; scenes that overlap in a transition must not share mutable state (cameras, glow targets).
5. Type must contrast with what's behind it — paper on dark, or a scrim (`createLinearGradient`) behind it.

**Verify like a picky editor**
- `npx anikit-render film.mjs --review review/` renders the film once at 10 samples/s and writes `sheet.jpg` (graded frames every 0.5 s with timestamps — the whole film in one image), `pacing.txt` (motion energy, **holds** where little moves for ≥ 1 s, flat frames, cuts) and `pacing.csv`. Look at the sheet; fix every hold the user didn't ask for.
- Preview at `--preview 15` and look at every frame; then render and pull strips around each cut/impact with ffmpeg (`-ss t -frames:v 14 -vf scale=240:-1,tile=14x1`).
- Watch for: empty or flat frames, type over same-tone content, shots that hold still for more than ~1 s.
- `ffprobe` the output: duration, frame count, and whether an audio stream should be there.
- `npx anikit-render --check film.mp4` compares every frame with the last and lists **spikes** (single-frame pops, things switching on in view, worker-slice seams) and frozen frames, with timestamps. Every spike should be a flash, cut or impact you placed; fix the rest (usually an item gated on by camera position while in frame).
- Slow render? `npx anikit-render film.mjs --profile` shows where each frame's time goes (your `step`/`draw` hooks, each `renderer3d` pass, the grade). Fix the biggest line first: fewer motion-blur samples on calm shots, `mirror` only where the floor is visible, gate heavy items by time.


---

# Anikit recipes

Task-oriented, copy-paste-ready examples. Every TypeScript block here is type-checked against the real API (`npm run typecheck`). The ones with an HTML fixture are loaded in happy-dom with no warnings allowed (`test/recipes.test.ts`), and in headless Chromium, where most are also clicked, dragged, hovered and scrolled with assertions (`npm run docs:browser`). The Python blocks run under pytest. Reference: [api.md](api.md).

Three rules cover most surprises:

1. **Times are seconds** (`duration: 0.6`, `stagger(0.05)`), except `engine.onFrame((timeMs, dtMs) => …)`.
2. **Use transforms** (`x`, `y`, `scale`, `rotate`) for motion, not `left`/`top`.
3. **Give a start value when it matters** (`opacity: [0, 1]`), and create animations for scroll triggers with `autoplay: false`.

Contents: [Hero entrance](#hero-entrance) · [Staggered list](#staggered-list) · [Reveal on scroll](#reveal-on-scroll) · [Scroll-scrubbed pinned section](#scroll-scrubbed-pinned-section) · [Page transition](#page-transition) · [Draggable carousel](#draggable-carousel) · [Physics toy](#physics-toy) · [SVG morph and line drawing](#svg-morph-and-line-drawing) · [Number counter](#number-counter) · [Hover and press](#hover-and-press) · [Pointer follower](#pointer-follower) · [Layout change (FLIP)](#layout-change-flip) · [Components and reduced motion](#components-and-reduced-motion) · [Testing an animation](#testing-an-animation) · [Recording a GIF or MP4](#recording-a-gif-or-mp4) · [Rendering a video in Node](#rendering-a-video-in-node) · [Python](#python)

---

## A whole landing page in a few calls

`recipe()` packs the common patterns (hero reveal, scroll story, magnetic buttons, scramble, counters, parallax, SVG drawing, tilt cards) behind one call each, with good defaults. Each returns a handle whose `revert()` undoes it.

```html
<header class="hero">
  <h1>Make it move</h1>
  <p>Every pattern on this page is one call.</p>
  <a class="cta" href="#more">Learn more</a>
</header>
<main id="more">
  <section><h2 class="code">DECODED</h2></section>
  <section><b class="stat">1200</b> <b class="stat">98</b></section>
  <div class="gallery"><img alt=""><img alt=""><img alt=""></div>
  <svg viewBox="0 0 100 20"><path d="M0 10 Q 25 0 50 10 T 100 10" fill="none" stroke="black"/></svg>
</main>
```

```ts
import { recipe, variants } from 'anikit';

recipe('hero-reveal', '.hero');                                // masked words rise, the rest fades up
recipe('magnetic-buttons', '.hero');                           // the CTA leans towards the cursor
recipe('scroll-story', 'main', { children: 'section' });       // each section rises in on scroll
recipe('text-scramble', '.code', { onScroll: true });          // decodes when it enters
recipe('count-up', '.stat');                                   // counts to the number written in it
recipe('parallax-gallery', '.gallery');                        // images drift at different depths
recipe('draw-svg', 'svg');                                     // strokes draw in on enter

// Named states with orchestration, for UI that toggles (menus, cards):
const cta = variants('.cta', { rest: { scale: 1 }, hot: { scale: 1.06, transition: { ease: 'spring(bounce: 0.5)' } } }, { initial: 'rest' });
document.querySelector('.cta')!.addEventListener('pointerenter', () => cta.animate('hot'));
document.querySelector('.cta')!.addEventListener('pointerleave', () => cta.animate('rest'));
```

- Options shared by every recipe: `duration`, `delay`, `stagger`, `ease`, `children`, `distance`, `strength`, `onScroll`, `once`; unknown keys warn with a "did you mean" and a link.
- Starting from nothing? `npx anikit new vanilla my-site` writes this page, ready to open.

## Hero entrance

Split the headline into characters, rise them in with a stagger, then bring in the rest with overlaps.

```html
<section class="hero">
  <h1 class="hero-title">Motion, compiled.</h1>
  <p class="hero-sub">A Rust/WebAssembly animation engine.</p>
  <a class="hero-cta" href="#start">Get started</a>
</section>
```

```ts
import { timeline, splitText, stagger } from 'anikit';

const { chars } = splitText('.hero-title', { type: 'words,chars' });   // words keep line breaks natural

timeline({ defaults: { ease: 'outCubic', duration: 0.6 } })
  .add(chars, { y: ['110%', 0], opacity: [0, 1] }, { delay: stagger(0.025) })
  .add('.hero-sub', { y: [16, 0], opacity: [0, 1] }, '-=0.35')          // overlap the previous step by 0.35 s
  .add('.hero-cta', { scale: [0.8, 1], opacity: [0, 1] }, { ease: 'spring(bounce: 0.4)' }, '-=0.2');
```

- `'-=0.35'` places a step relative to the end of the timeline; `'<'` starts with the previous step, `'label+=0.2'` after a label.
- Hide the hero with CSS (`opacity: 0`) only if you also give explicit start values like above, so there is no flash before the script runs.

## Staggered list

Items enter one after another; a removed item animates out before it leaves the DOM.

```html
<ul class="todo">
  <li>Write the docs</li>
  <li>Test the recipes</li>
  <li>Ship it</li>
</ul>
```

```ts
import { animate, stagger } from 'anikit';

animate('.todo li', { x: [-24, 0], opacity: [0, 1] }, { duration: 0.5, ease: 'outCubic', delay: stagger(0.06) });

export async function removeItem(li: HTMLElement) {
  await animate(li, { x: 40, opacity: 0, height: 0 }, { duration: 0.3, ease: 'inQuad' });   // await = finished
  li.remove();
}

export function addItem(list: HTMLElement, text: string) {
  const li = document.createElement('li');
  li.textContent = text;
  list.append(li);
  animate(li, { y: [12, 0], opacity: [0, 1] }, { duration: 0.4, ease: 'outBack' });
}
```

- `stagger(0.06, { from: 'center' })` ripples from the middle; `{ grid: [cols, rows] }` for grids.
- A new animation on the same property takes it over, so `removeItem` during the entrance is safe.

## Reveal on scroll

Each card plays when it enters the viewport and reverses when you scroll back above it.

```html
<div class="card reveal">One</div>
<div class="card reveal">Two</div>
<div class="card reveal">Three</div>
```

```ts
import { animate, scrollTriggerBatch } from 'anikit';

scrollTriggerBatch('.reveal', {
  start: 'top 85%',                              // when the card's top passes 85% down the viewport
  toggleActions: 'play none none reverse',       // onEnter onLeave onEnterBack onLeaveBack
  animation: (el) => animate(el, { y: [40, 0], opacity: [0, 1] }, { duration: 0.6, ease: 'outCubic', autoplay: false }),
});
```

Simpler, one-shot, without scroll math:

```ts
import { animate, inView } from 'anikit';

inView('.reveal', (el) => {
  animate(el, { y: [40, 0], opacity: [0, 1] }, { duration: 0.6 });
}, { amount: 0.3, once: true });
```

## Scroll-scrubbed pinned section

The section pins while its timeline follows the scrollbar, then releases. A progress bar tracks the whole page.

```html
<div class="progress"></div>
<section class="story">
  <div class="panel a">A</div>
  <div class="panel b">B</div>
</section>
<section class="after">Next</section>
```

```ts
import { scrollTrigger, timeline, scroll, animate } from 'anikit';

const tl = timeline({ autoplay: false, defaults: { ease: 'none' } })
  .add('.story .a', { x: [0, -300], opacity: [1, 0] })
  .add('.story .b', { x: [300, 0], opacity: [0, 1] }, '<')     // '<' = same start as the previous step
  .label('done');

scrollTrigger({
  trigger: '.story',
  start: 'top top',        // section top meets viewport top
  end: '+=1200',           // 1200 px of scrolling
  pin: true,
  scrub: 0.4,              // follow the scrollbar with 0.4 s of smoothing
  snap: { to: 'labels', duration: 0.3 },
  animation: tl,
});

scroll(animate('.progress', { scaleX: [0, 1] }, { ease: 'linear', autoplay: false }));   // whole-page progress
```

- Positions are `"<trigger edge> <viewport edge>"` with `top`/`center`/`bottom`, `%` or `px`, e.g. `'top 80%'`, `'center center'`, `'bottom+=100 top'`.
- After you change layout yourself (images loaded, content injected), call `refreshScrollTriggers()`.
- Pinning and scrubbing need real layout: check them in a browser (Playwright works headless), not in happy-dom/jsdom.

## Page transition

Fade the current page out, swap, fade the next in. `await` works on every animation and timeline.

```html
<main>
  <section class="page active" id="home">Home <a href="#about" data-to="about">About</a></section>
  <section class="page" id="about" style="display: none">About <a href="#home" data-to="home">Home</a></section>
</main>
```

```ts
import { animate } from 'anikit';

let busy = false;
async function show(id: string) {
  const current = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.page.active');
  const next = document.getElementById(id);
  if (busy || !current || !next || current === next) return;
  busy = true;
  await animate(current, { opacity: [1, 0], y: [0, -16] }, { duration: 0.25, ease: 'inQuad' });
  current.classList.remove('active');
  current.style.display = 'none';
  next.style.display = '';
  next.classList.add('active');
  await animate(next, { opacity: [0, 1], y: [16, 0] }, { duration: 0.4, ease: 'outCubic' });
  busy = false;
}

document.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
  const link = (e.target as Element).closest<HTMLElement>('[data-to]');
  if (link) {
    e.preventDefault();
    void show(link.dataset.to!);
  }
});
```

For full-page "one section per swipe" navigation, `observer({ onDown, onUp, tolerance: 20 })` turns wheel, touch and pointer input into intents.

## Shader transition on real DOM (shatter, dissolve, curl)

Break a card apart on click, then bring it back. `htmlEffect` draws the element into a WebGL overlay (natively where the browser supports HTML-in-Canvas, through SVG `foreignObject` elsewhere), animates the effect and restores the element. Clicks still reach the real element while the effect plays.

```html
<div class="notice" style="width:280px;padding:20px;border-radius:14px;background:#24324d;color:#fff">
  <strong>Saved!</strong> Your changes are live.
  <button class="dismiss">Dismiss</button>
</div>
<button class="restore">Restore</button>
```

```ts
import { htmlEffect } from 'anikit';

const notice = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.notice')!;
document.querySelector('.dismiss')!.addEventListener('click', async () => {
  await htmlEffect(notice, 'shatter', { duration: 1.2 }).finished; // notice is now visibility: hidden
});
document.querySelector('.restore')!.addEventListener('click', () => {
  htmlEffect(notice, 'dissolve', { mode: 'in', duration: 0.8, color: '#7cf' }); // reveal it again
});
```

## Draggable carousel

Drag (or throw) the track; it settles on a slide. Buttons animate to the neighbouring slide.

```html
<div class="carousel" style="overflow: hidden; width: 320px">
  <div class="track" style="display: flex; width: 960px">
    <div class="slide" style="width: 320px">1</div>
    <div class="slide" style="width: 320px">2</div>
    <div class="slide" style="width: 320px">3</div>
  </div>
  <button class="prev">‹</button>
  <button class="next">›</button>
</div>
```

```ts
import { draggable, animate } from 'anikit';

const track = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.track')!;
const width = 320;
const count = track.children.length;
let index = 0;

draggable(track, {
  type: 'x',
  bounds: { minX: -(count - 1) * width, maxX: 0 },   // transform px; or an element: bounds: '.carousel'
  inertia: true,                                     // throw with momentum…
  snap: { x: width },                                // …and come to rest on a slide
  edgeResistance: 0.5,
  onThrowUpdate: (d) => { index = Math.round(-d.x / width); },   // follow the glide to its slide
});

const go = (dir: number) => {
  index = Math.max(0, Math.min(count - 1, index + dir));
  animate(track, { x: -index * width }, { duration: 0.5, ease: 'outCubic' });
};
document.querySelector('.prev')!.addEventListener('click', () => go(-1));
document.querySelector('.next')!.addEventListener('click', () => go(1));
```

`draggable()` returns an array (one `Draggable` per element): `const [drag] = draggable(el)`. It reads the element's transform on every press, so animating `x` from the buttons and dragging mix freely; keep your own `index` (a `Draggable`'s `x` only updates while it is pressed or thrown).

## Physics toy

DOM elements fall, collide, and can be grabbed and thrown; the pointer pushes them away.

```html
<div id="stage" style="position: relative; width: 600px; height: 400px">
  <div class="ball" style="position: absolute; width: 40px; height: 40px; border-radius: 50%"></div>
  <div class="ball" style="position: absolute; width: 60px; height: 60px; border-radius: 50%"></div>
  <div class="wall" style="position: absolute; left: 200px; top: 300px; width: 200px; height: 20px"></div>
</div>
```

```ts
import { world } from 'anikit';

const w = world({ container: '#stage', gravity: [0, 980], restitution: 0.4, friction: 0.05 });
w.bind('#stage .ball', { rotate: true });   // elements become circular bodies; transforms follow
w.obstacles('#stage .wall');                // element boxes become static colliders
w.dragging();                               // grab and throw
w.pointer({ mode: 'repel', radius: 120 });  // or 'attract'
```

For thousands of bodies, skip the DOM: `w.addMany([...])` and `w.draw(ctx)` on a canvas, or read `w.data` (`[x, y, angle]` per body). Units are px and seconds; `engine.speed = 0.2` gives slow motion.

## SVG morph and line drawing

```html
<svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="200" height="200">
  <path id="shape" d="M50,10 L90,90 L10,90 Z" fill="currentColor" />
  <path id="line" d="M10,50 C30,10 70,90 90,50" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" />
</svg>
```

```ts
import { animate, timeline, star, circle } from 'anikit';

// Morph through several shapes (any path data, element or selector; point counts may differ).
animate('#shape', { d: [null, star(50, 50, 5, 40, 18), circle(50, 50, 40)] }, { duration: 2.4, ease: 'inOutCubic', repeat: Infinity, yoyo: true });

// Draw the stroke in, then out from the other end.
timeline({ repeat: Infinity, repeatDelay: 0.5 })
  .add('#line', { draw: [0, 1] }, { duration: 1.2, ease: 'inOutCubic' })
  .add('#line', { draw: ['0 1', '1 1'] }, { duration: 0.8, ease: 'inCubic' });
```

Motion along a path: `animate('#dot', { path: { path: '#line', rotate: true } }, { duration: 3, ease: 'linear' })`.

## Number counter

Count up when the number scrolls into view, formatted as currency.

```html
<p>Revenue: <span id="revenue">$0</span></p>
```

```ts
import { animate, inView } from 'anikit';

inView('#revenue', (el) => {
  animate(el, { textContent: [0, 128400] }, {
    duration: 1.6,
    ease: 'outExpo',
    format: { style: 'currency', currency: 'USD', maximumFractionDigits: 0 },
    locale: 'en-US',
  });
}, { once: true });
```

The preset does the same: `effects.countUp('#revenue', { to: 128400, format: { style: 'currency', currency: 'USD' } })`. Without `format`, use `round: true` for whole numbers.

## Hover and press

```html
<button class="btn">Buy now</button>
```

```ts
import { hover, press, spring } from 'anikit';

hover('.btn', (el) => {
  spring(el, { scale: 1.06, y: -2 }, { stiffness: 400, damping: 22 });
  return () => spring(el, { scale: 1, y: 0 }, { stiffness: 400, damping: 22 });   // runs on leave
});
press('.btn', (el) => {
  spring(el, { scale: 0.94 }, { stiffness: 600, damping: 30 });
  return () => spring(el, { scale: 1.06 }, { stiffness: 400, damping: 15 });      // runs on release
});
```

`spring()` retargets the running spring and keeps its velocity, so fast hover in/out never jumps. `hover` ignores touch, so nothing sticks on phones.

## Pointer follower

```html
<div class="dot" style="position: fixed; left: 0; top: 0; width: 16px; height: 16px; border-radius: 50%"></div>
```

```ts
import { spring, quickTo } from 'anikit';

// Springy, with momentum:
addEventListener('pointermove', (e) => {
  spring('.dot', { x: e.clientX - 8, y: e.clientY - 8 }, { stiffness: 300, damping: 25 });
});

// Or a plain eased chase, one function per property (cheap to call every event):
const toX = quickTo('.dot', 'x', { duration: 0.4, ease: 'outCubic' });
const toY = quickTo('.dot', 'y', { duration: 0.4, ease: 'outCubic' });
addEventListener('pointermove', (e) => { toX(e.clientX - 8); toY(e.clientY - 8); });
```

## One value driving many properties (slider, scroll, marquee)

```html
<input id="amount" type="range" min="0" max="1" step="0.001" value="0" />
<div class="card" style="width: 120px; height: 80px; background: #6ea8ff"></div>
<div class="logos" style="display: flex; gap: 40px"><span>Northwind</span><span>Acme</span><span>Globex</span></div>
```

```ts
import { motionValue, bindValues, scrollProgress, marquee, magnetic } from 'anikit';

// One source of truth; every property follows it (springy when the slider moves).
const amount = motionValue(0);
bindValues('.card', {
  x: amount.map([0, 1], [0, 400]),
  rotate: amount.map([0, 1], [0, 90], { ease: 'inOutCubic' }),
  opacity: amount.map([0, 0.5, 1], [0.4, 1, 0.4]),
});
document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('#amount')!.addEventListener('input', (e) => {
  amount.spring(+(e.target as HTMLInputElement).value, { stiffness: 180, damping: 16 });
});

// Page scroll as a value: the card shrinks a little as you scroll.
bindValues('.card', { scale: scrollProgress().map([0, 1], [1, 0.8]) });

// An endless logo row that pauses on hover and speeds up with scrolling, and a magnetic card.
marquee('.logos', { speed: 60, pauseOnHover: true, scrollBoost: 0.5 });
magnetic('.card', { strength: 0.3 });
```

`bindValues()` writes on every change (transforms compose with other animations), and everything here is undone by `context().revert()`.

## Layout change (FLIP)

Change the layout however you like; `flip()` animates elements from where they were.

```html
<div class="grid">
  <div class="item">1</div>
  <div class="item">2</div>
  <div class="item">3</div>
</div>
<button class="toggle">Toggle</button>
```

```ts
import { flip } from 'anikit';

const grid = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.grid')!;
document.querySelector('.toggle')!.addEventListener('click', () => {
  flip('.grid .item', () => grid.classList.toggle('dense'), { duration: 0.6, ease: 'spring(bounce: 0.2)' });
});
```

For changes that happen later (after a fetch, in a framework render), split it: `const state = flip.capture('.item')`, update, then `flip.from(state, options)`.

## Components and reduced motion

Collect everything a component creates, scope selectors to it, and undo it all on unmount. Honour the OS "reduce motion" setting once at startup.

```html
<div id="app"><div class="card">A</div><div class="card">B</div></div>
```

```ts
import { context, animate, stagger, scrollTrigger, engine, matchMedia } from 'anikit';

engine.reducedMotion = 'user';     // animations jump to their end state when the OS asks for less motion

export function mount(root: HTMLElement) {
  const ctx = context(() => {
    animate('.card', { y: [24, 0], opacity: [0, 1] }, { delay: stagger(0.05) });   // only .card inside root
    scrollTrigger({ trigger: root, start: 'top 80%', onEnter: () => root.classList.add('seen') });
  }, root);
  return () => ctx.revert();       // kills animations/triggers and restores inline styles
}

const unmount = mount(document.getElementById('app')!);

// Responsive: set up while a query matches, reverted automatically when it stops matching.
matchMedia().add('(min-width: 800px)', () => {
  animate('.card', { rotate: [-2, 0] });
});
```

React: call `mount(ref.current)` in `useLayoutEffect` and return the cleanup. Vue: `onMounted` / `onUnmounted`. Svelte: an action that returns `{ destroy }`.

## Testing an animation

Deterministic, no `requestAnimationFrame`, works in vitest/jest with happy-dom or jsdom.

```html
<body></body>
```

```ts
import { animate, testing, engine } from 'anikit';

await testing.ready;
testing.useFakeTime();                        // time moves only when you advance it
const warnings = testing.captureWarnings();   // collect "anikit:" warnings; call before the code under test

const el = document.createElement('div');
document.body.append(el);
animate(el, { x: 100, opacity: [0, 1] }, { duration: 1, ease: 'linear' });

testing.advance(0.5);                         // seconds, in 60 fps frames
console.assert(el.style.transform === 'translate(50px,0px)');
console.assert(engine.inspect()[0].progress === 0.5);
testing.finishAll();                          // run until idle
console.assert(el.style.opacity === '1');
console.assert(warnings.length === 0);
testing.reset();                              // between tests
```

In a real browser (Playwright), `window.__ANIKIT__` is the engine: `__ANIKIT__.manual(true)`, `__ANIKIT__.tick(16.67)`, `__ANIKIT__.inspect()`.

## Recording a GIF or MP4

In the page (frame-exact; time is advanced exactly `1 / fps` per frame):

```html
<div id="stage" style="position: relative; width: 360px; height: 80px; background: #111">
  <div class="box" style="width: 40px; height: 40px; background: #f60"></div>
</div>
```

```ts browser
import { record, screenshot, timeline } from 'anikit';

const tl = timeline({ autoplay: false }).add('#stage .box', { x: [0, 300] }, { duration: 2 });
const gif = await record('#stage', { duration: 2, fps: 30, animation: tl });   // seek tl per frame
gif.download('stage.gif');

const webm = await record('#stage', { duration: 2, format: 'webm' });
const png: Blob = await screenshot('#stage');
console.log(webm.frames, png.size);
```

From the command line, headless (needs `npm i -D playwright && npx playwright install chromium`; MP4/WebM need ffmpeg):

```bash
npx anikit-record ./index.html --out hero.gif --duration 3 --fps 30 --selector '#hero'
npx anikit-record http://localhost:5173 --out clip.mp4 --size 1280x720
npx anikit-record ./index.html --screenshot shot.png --at 1.5
```

## Rendering a video in Node

For films, trailers and title sequences rendered without a browser (Skia + ffmpeg; `npm i @napi-rs/canvas`). Start from the template, look at stills, then render:

```bash
npx anikit-render --init film.mjs                     # a working starter
npx anikit-render film.mjs --still 1.5 --out f.png    # one frame, fast
npx anikit-render film.mjs --preview 15 --out pv/     # every 15th frame as JPEG
npx anikit-render film.mjs --out film.mp4 --workers 4
```

A minimal composition module:

```js
// title.mjs: default-export a function that returns a composition
export default async function film({ anikit }) {
  const { composition, typeFx } = anikit;
  const film = composition({ width: 1280, height: 720, fps: 30, duration: 3 });
  film.scene('title', 0, 3, {
    draw({ ctx, t, width, height }) {
      ctx.fillStyle = '#0b0c10';
      ctx.fillRect(0, 0, width, height);
      typeFx(ctx, 'Hello, anikit.', width / 2, height / 2, { t, start: 0.3, effect: 'rise', size: 96, color: '#f4efe6', align: 'center' });
    },
  });
  return film;
}
```

Keep films deterministic: start tweens in a scene's `enter()`, advance simulations in `step({ dt })`, and only read state in `draw()`. `Math.random` is seeded; don't use `Date.now()`. See [Video: compositions](api.md#video-compositions).

## A 3D fly-through film (that doesn't look plain)

Start from the template — it already wires everything below — then change the world and the route:

```bash
npx anikit-render --init fly.mjs --template journey
npx anikit-render fly.mjs --review review/      # sheet.jpg + pacing.txt: look before you render
npx anikit-render fly.mjs --out fly.mp4         # 1080p60 across all cores, with a progress line
```

The pieces, in the order a frame is built:

```js
// fly.mjs
export default async ({ anikit: A }) => {
  const { composition, scene3d, renderer3d, mesh, instances, flightPath } = A;
  const W = 1920, H = 1080;
  const cam = scene3d({ fov: 64, width: W, height: H, near: 4, far: 40000 });
  const r3 = renderer3d({ width: W, height: H });
  // 1. A route and a speed curve. Fractions of the path over seconds; it never stops until the end.
  const path = flightPath([[0, 400, 3000], [0, 80, -3000], [250, 120, -9000], [0, 150, -20000]], { lookAhead: 900, bank: 1.3 });
  const s = path.timing([[0, 0], [2, 0.4], [4, 0.75], [6, 1]]);
  // 2. The world: dark bodies, colour in light.
  // Meshes and instances are created once, outside draw().
  const towers = instances(400, (i) => ({ x: (i % 2 ? 1 : -1) * (300 + (i * 37) % 900), y: 300, z: -Math.floor(i / 2) * 150, sx: 100, sy: 1200, sz: 100, color: [0.03, 0.035, 0.05] }));
  const cube = mesh.cube(), floor = mesh.plane(1);
  const floorAt = instances(1, () => ({ y: -300, z: -10000, sx: 12000, sz: 30000, color: [0.02, 0.02, 0.03] }));
  const film = composition({ width: W, height: H, fps: 60, duration: 6, motionBlur: 1,
    post: { aa: 1, bloom: 0.9, bloomThreshold: 0.5, streaks: 0.5, rays: 0.8, flares: 0.5, vignette: 0.45, grain: 4, contrast: 1.06 } });
  let prev = 0, last = 0;
  film.scene('fly', 0, 6, {
    step: ({ clock }) => { prev = last; last = clock; },       // clock: scene seconds, slowed by timeScale
    draw: ({ ctx, clock }) => {
      path.apply(cam, s(prev)); const prevCamera = cam.viewProjection().matrix;
      path.apply(cam, s(clock));
      const px = r3.render(cam, [
        { mirror: true, mesh: floor, instances: floorAt, material: { lines: 1.4, lineColor: [0.3, 0.55, 1.6], grid: [60, 150], lineWidth: 0.03 } },
        { mesh: cube, instances: towers, material: { metal: 0.6, lines: 1.6, pattern: 'hex', grid: [3, 12], lineColor: [1.6, 0.3, 1], pulse: 2, pulsePhase: clock * 2 } },
      ], { background: '#03040a', fog: [8000, 24000], fogColor: [0.18, 0.06, 0.2], sky: [0.02, 0.02, 0.08], horizon: [0.95, 0.35, 0.7], ground: [0.01, 0.01, 0.02],
           strips: [1.8, 1.8, 2.2], key: [0, 0.14, -1], keyColor: [1, 0.7, 0.9], skybox: { sun: 2.2 }, mirror: { y: -300, strength: 0.45 }, motionBlur: { shutter: 0.55 }, prevCamera });
      ctx.putImageData(new globalThis.ImageData(px, W, H), 0, 0);
    },
  });
  return film;
};
```

What makes it look expensive rather than plain:

- **Near-black bodies, colour in light.** Base colours around `[0.03, 0.035, 0.05]`; the colour comes from `lines` / `pattern` (`'hex'`, `'circuit'`, `'dots'`), `pulse`, `emissive`, chrome (`metal` + `strips`) and bloom. Flat-coloured lit shapes read as placeholder art.
- **Two or three hues per shot.** One warm, one cool, one neutral. The sky (`skybox`), the fog colour and the horizon should be the same family so geometry dissolves into the distance.
- **Speed you can feel.** `motionBlur` on the render (with `prevCamera`, so previews match the final render), stars as `points` with a small `streak`, light trails (`mesh.tube` along `path.points()`, `blend: 'additive'`, `pulse`), objects passing close to the camera. Bank into turns (`bank`), add a barrel roll (`path.apply(cam, s, rollDegrees)`).
- **Something always changes.** `--review` flags any stretch of ≥ 1 s with little motion. Fix every hold you didn't intend: speed up, cut closer to geometry, add a pulse wave or a hit.
- **Hits land.** `film.impact(t, { shake, flash, aberration, shockwave })` plus a `timeScale` dip right after (bullet time) and a `shatter()` of the object you hit.
- **Know where the time goes.** `npx anikit-render fly.mjs --profile` prints each frame's cost per 3D pass and for the grade; fix the biggest line first.
- **One hero at the end.** `mesh.text(name, { font })` in chrome on the mirror floor, the sun behind it, `rays` aimed at the sun, the camera settling (ease the last metres, then hold ~1.5 s).

Pitfalls that cost a render:

- **Bullet time shifts every later beat.** Choreograph on the scene clock (`FrameInfo.clock`, or your own sum of `dt`), and place impacts with `film.timeAt('scene', clockSeconds)`: a 0.6 s dip moves everything after it by 0.6 s of composition time. `post` functions receive composition time; convert with `film.clockAt('scene', t)`.
- **Unwind roll the short way.** Barrel rolls add up (three rolls = 1080°). Before easing `cam.roll` back to level for a landing, wrap it: `cam.roll = ((((cam.roll + 180) % 360) + 360) % 360 - 180) * (1 - k)`, otherwise the camera spins three times on arrival.
- **End the route past the last stop.** `path.apply()` at the very end of a path has nothing to look ahead at. Add one waypoint beyond where the camera stops, and stop the timing short of it.
- **`pulse` is two things.** Any `pulse > 0` makes the pattern's lines flare as the pulse passes; the value itself is how strongly the *whole surface* glows with it. On large patterned bodies (towers, walls) keep it small (≈ 0.3–0.5) so the light runs along the lines; save big values for trails, rings and hero objects.
- **Metal reflects the horizon.** Large `metal` faces mirror the sky, so a bright `horizon` turns them into flat slabs of colour. Keep big bodies at `metal` ≤ 0.3 and save chrome for heroes (gates, knots, type).

## Python

The Python package animates plain objects (dicts, objects, lists of them) with the same engine. Times are seconds; options are keyword arguments in `snake_case`.

```python
import anikit

box = {"x": 0, "opacity": 0, "color": "#ff0000"}
anikit.animate(box, {"x": 100, "opacity": [0, 1], "color": "royalblue"}, duration=0.6, ease="outBack")

for frame, t in anikit.render(fps=30):      # advances the engine and writes values until idle
    pass
assert box["x"] == 100 and box["opacity"] == 1
```

Timelines: in Python the **position is the third positional argument** and options are keywords (in TypeScript, options come third).

```python
import anikit

a, b = {"x": 0}, {"y": 0}
tl = anikit.timeline(defaults={"duration": 0.5, "ease": "outCubic"})
tl.add(a, {"x": 100})
tl.add(b, {"y": 50}, "-=0.25")             # overlap the previous step
tl.label("end").call(lambda: print("done"), "end")
anikit.run_until_idle()
assert (a["x"], b["y"]) == (100, 50)
```

Springs, staggers and export to CSS:

```python
import anikit

dots = [{"x": 0} for _ in range(5)]
anikit.animate(dots, {"x": 200}, duration=0.8, delay=anikit.stagger(0.05, from_="center"))   # from_: `from` is a keyword in Python
anikit.spring({"scale": 1}, {"scale": 1.5}, stiffness=300, damping=20)
anikit.run_until_idle()

anim = anikit.animate({"x": 0, "opacity": 0}, {"x": 100, "opacity": 1}, duration=0.6, ease="spring(bounce: 0.3)", autoplay=False)
css = anim.to_css_keyframes("enter", selector=".card")    # @keyframes + a rule
print(css.splitlines()[0])
```

Physics world (no DOM): step it yourself and read positions.

```python
import anikit

world = anikit.World(gravity=(0, 980), bounds=(0, 0, 800, 600), restitution=0.3)
balls = [world.add_body(100 + i * 30, 50, radius=10) for i in range(10)]
world.run(2.0)                              # 2 simulated seconds at 60 fps (or world.step(dt) per frame)
print(round(balls[0].x), round(balls[0].y))
```

`world.bind(body, sprite)` (or `body.bind(sprite)`) writes a body's `x`, `y` and `rotation` into a dict or object after every step, like the DOM binding in TypeScript.


---

# Anikit TypeScript API

Times are in **seconds**. Every function accepts targets as a CSS selector, an element, a list/NodeList, a plain object, or an array mixing these.

```ts
import { animate, timeline, stagger, spring, inertia, scroll, inView, splitText, flip,
         compositor, batch, set, from, fromTo, engine, ready } from 'anikit';
// or: import ... from 'anikit/lean'  (streams anikit.wasm instead of embedding it)
// or: import ... from 'anikit/tween' (animate, timeline, stagger, spring, inertia only: ~121 KB min+gzip with its core)
```

The WebAssembly core starts compiling on import. Calls made before it's ready are queued and run in order, so you rarely need it, but `await ready` is available. Functions that return a computed value right away (`ease()`, `morph()`, `pathLength()`, `staggerValues()`, `world()`, …) need the core loaded: with `anikit/lean`, `await init()` (or `await ready`) first.

**Units:** times are **seconds** everywhere (`duration`, `delay`, `stagger(0.05)`, `seek(1.2)`), except the low-level clock: `engine.tick(ms)`, `engine.time` and `engine.onFrame((timeMs, dtMs) => …)` are milliseconds. Numbers default to `px` for lengths, `deg` for angles; `scale` and `opacity` are unitless (opacity 0–1).

Task-oriented examples: [recipes.md](recipes.md). One-call patterns: [`recipe()`](#recipes-recipe). Feature comparison with GSAP, Motion and anime.js: [parity.md](parity.md). Every options object as JSON Schema (descriptions included): [api.schema.json](api.schema.json), also shipped as `anikit/api.schema.json` (regenerate with `npm run schema`). Mistakes are reported as `anikit:` warnings with fixes (see [Testing and diagnostics](#testing-and-diagnostics)).

---

## `animate(targets, keyframes, options?) → Animation`

```ts
animate('.box', { x: 200, rotate: 45, backgroundColor: '#0af' }, { duration: 0.6, ease: 'outBack' });
animate(el, { opacity: [0, 1], y: [20, 0] });                     // from → to
animate(el, { x: [0, 100, 50] }, { times: [0, 0.3, 1] });          // keyframes
animate(el, [{ x: 0 }, { x: 100, offset: 0.2, ease: 'inQuad' }, { x: 0 }]); // WAAPI-style list
animate(el, { x: { to: 100, ease: 'outElastic' }, y: '+=50' });  // per-property easing, relative
animate(els, { x: (el, i, n) => i * 20 }, { delay: stagger(0.05, { from: 'center' }) });
animate(obj, { value: 1 }, { onUpdate: () => render(obj.value) }); // plain objects
```

**Values:** numbers (with the default unit: `px` for lengths, `deg` for angles), strings with units, colours in any CSS syntax, complex strings (`'0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,.2)'`), discrete strings, `null` for "the current value", relative values (`'+=10'`, `'-=10'`, `'*=2'`) and `(target, index, count) => value` functions (which may return keyframes: `y: (el, i) => [0, i * 10]`). Options may also be written inside the keyframes object (GSAP style).

**Special properties**

| Property | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `x y z translateX/Y/Z rotate rotateX/Y/Z scale scaleX/Y/Z skew skewX/Y perspective` | Transform components, composed into one `transform` per element per frame. |
| `'--name'` | CSS custom property. |
| `attr: { r: 20, cx: 50 }` | Attributes. Non‑CSS attributes of SVG elements are detected automatically. |
| `d: pathData \| element \| selector` | Shape morph between any two paths. |
| `path: pathData \| { path, start?, end?, rotate?, align?, alignOrigin? }` | Motion along a path. `rotate: true` (or an angle offset) follows the tangent. `align: true` puts the target exactly on the path as drawn on the page (SVG user space, viewBox and all, mapped to the target's coordinates), with `alignOrigin` (default `[0.5, 0.5]`) on the line; pass an SVG element as `align` when `path` is raw data in its coordinates. |
| `draw: [0, 1]` or `['0 0', '0.2 0.8']` | Visible stroke segment as fractions of the length. |

**Options** (`AnimateOptions`)

| Option | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `duration` | `0.5` | Seconds. Spring easings default to their natural settle time. Accepts a function per target. |
| `delay` | `0` | Seconds, a function, or `stagger()`. |
| `ease` | `'outQuad'` | An easing (see below), or an array with one easing per keyframe segment. |
| `repeat`, `repeatDelay`, `yoyo`, `direction` | | `repeat: Infinity` (or `-1`) loops. |
| `speed` | `1` | Playback rate. Negative plays backwards. |
| `times` | | Keyframe offsets for array values. |
| `colorSpace` | `'oklab'` | `'srgb' \| 'linear' \| 'oklab' \| 'oklch' \| 'hsl'`. |
| `fillMode` | `'both'` | `'forwards' \| 'backwards' \| 'none'` (named `fillMode` so `fill` stays the SVG/CSS property). |
| `overwrite` | `true` | A new animation takes over the properties it animates. |
| `immediateRender` | auto | Render the first keyframe right away. Defaults to on for delayed animations with explicit start values. |
| `autoplay` | `true` | `false` for scroll triggers and manual control. |
| `stagger` | | Shorthand for `delay: stagger(n)`; GSAP's `{ each, from, grid, amount }` works too. |
| `loop` | | `true` repeats forever (`repeat: Infinity`). |
| `onStart`, `onUpdate`, `onComplete`, `onRepeat`, `onReverseComplete` | | `onUpdate` fires once per frame, after DOM writes. |

`from(targets, values, options)`, `fromTo(targets, fromValues, toValues, options)` and `set(targets, values)` (instant) are shorthands.

```ts
from('.card', { y: 40, opacity: 0 });                            // from these values to the current ones
fromTo('.bar', { scaleX: 0 }, { scaleX: 1 }, { duration: 0.8 });
set('.panel', { x: -20, opacity: 0 });                           // instantly, no animation
```

### Controller (`Animation`, `Timeline`, `Batch`)

`play()`, `pause()`, `reverse()`, `restart()`, `seek(seconds)`, `complete()` (jump to the end), `cancel()` (pause and return to the start), `kill()`/`stop()` (stop where it is), `revert()` (stop and restore the original inline styles). Properties: `progress` (get/set, 0–1), `time` (get/set, seconds), `duration`, `speed` (get/set), `state` (`'idle' | 'running' | 'paused' | 'finished'`) and `iteration`. Controllers are thenables: `await animate(...)`, or use `.finished`. All of these are `Playable`s.

```ts
const a = animate('.box', { x: 200 }, { duration: 1, autoplay: false });
a.progress = 0.5;            // scrub by hand
await a.play();              // resolves when finished
const css = a.toCSS({ name: 'slide', selector: '.box' });   // see "Bake to CSS"

// The classes, for types and instanceof checks:
const all: Array<Animation | Timeline | Batch> = [a, timeline(), batch(10, { x: [0, 1] })];
all.forEach((c) => c.pause());
const s: PhysicsAnimation = spring('.dot', { x: 100 });
const c: CompositorAnimation = compositor('.toast', { opacity: [0, 1] });
await Promise.all([s, c]);   // both are awaitable too
```

`spring()`, `inertia()` and `physics()` return a `PhysicsAnimation` (`velocity`, `finished`, `then`, `kill()`/`stop()`, `revert()`); `compositor()` returns a `CompositorAnimation` (`play`, `pause`, `reverse`, `seek`, `speed`, `progress`, `kill`, `finished`).

---

## Easings

Accepted everywhere an `ease` is:

- **CSS:** `'linear'`, `'ease'`, `'ease-in-out'`, `'cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)'`, `'steps(4, jump-start)'`, `'step-end'`, `'linear(0, 0.25 75%, 1)'`.
- **Penner/Motion names:** `'inQuad'`, `'easeOutCubic'`, `'inOutQuart'`, `'outQuint'`, `'inSine'`, `'outExpo'`, `'circIn'`, `'outBack'`, `'inOutElastic'`, `'outBounce'`, plus `outIn*` variants.
- **GSAP names:** `'power1'`–`'power4'`, `'sine'`, `'expo'`, `'circ'`, `'back(1.7)'`, `'elastic(1, 0.3)'`, `'bounce'` with `.in`, `.out` or `.inOut`; `'pow(3).in'`.
- **Springs:** `'spring'`, `'spring(stiffness, damping, mass, velocity)'`, `'spring(bounce: 0.3, duration: 0.6)'`, or an object `{ stiffness, damping, mass }` / `{ bounce, duration }`.
- **Extras:** `'wiggle(5)'`, `'shake(8)'`, `'slowmo(0.7, 0.7)'`, `'anticipate'`.
- **Other forms:** a `[x1, y1, x2, y2]` bezier array, or any `(t) => number` function (sampled once into a 1024‑point table).

Helpers: `ease(e, t)`, `easing(e) → (t) => number`, and `cssEasing(e)` (native CSS string; springs become `linear()`).

```ts
ease('outCubic', 0.5);                       // 0.875
const bounce = easing('spring(bounce: 0.3)');   // (t) => number, for your own maths
el.style.transition = `transform 0.6s ${cssEasing('spring(bounce: 0.3)')}`;   // 'linear(…)' ('ease-out' where linear() is unsupported)
```

Unknown names throw with a suggestion (`'outCubik'` → "Did you mean "outCubic"?"). In TypeScript, `EasingName` autocompletes every named easing while any string is still accepted.

---

## Stagger

`stagger(each, options?)` returns a function value: use it for `delay` (seconds between targets) or any numeric property.

```ts
import { animate, stagger } from 'anikit';
animate('.cell', { scale: [0, 1] }, { delay: stagger(0.04, { grid: [10, 6], from: 'center' }) });   // ripples out of the middle
animate('.bar', { y: [40, 0] }, { delay: stagger(0.05, { start: 0.3, ease: 'inQuad' }) });          // base delay + eased spread
animate('.dot', { x: stagger(20) });                                                                // 0, 20, 40 … px
```

Options: `from` (`'first'` default, `'last'`, `'center'`, `'edges'`, `'random'` or an index), `grid: [columns, rows]` with optional `axis: 'x' | 'y'`, `total` (spread over this many seconds instead of `each` per step), `start` (added to every value), `ease` (across the distribution), `seed` (for `'random'`). `staggerValues(count, each, options)` returns the numbers directly:

```ts
staggerValues(4, 0.1, { from: 'center' });    // [0.15, 0.05, 0.05, 0.15]
```

---

## `timeline(options?) → Timeline`

```ts
const tl = timeline({ defaults: { duration: 0.4, ease: 'outCubic' }, repeat: 1, yoyo: true })
  .add('.title', { y: [30, 0], opacity: [0, 1] })
  .add('.item', { x: [-20, 0], opacity: [0, 1] }, { delay: stagger(0.05) }, '-=0.2')
  .label('spin')
  .add(logo, { rotate: 360 }, {}, 'spin+=0.1')
  .add(otherTimelineOrAnimation, '<')
  .call(() => console.log('halfway'), '>')
  .set(el, { display: 'none' });
tl.seek('spin'); tl.playFrom(0.5);
```

**Positions:**
- a number of seconds;
- `'<'` / `'>'`: start or end of the previous child, with an optional offset (`'<0.2'`, `'>-0.1'`);
- `'+=0.5'` / `'-=0.5'`: relative to the timeline end;
- a label, optionally with an offset (`'label'`, `'label+=0.3'`).

With no position, a child goes at the end of the timeline. The position may also go straight after the properties, GSAP style: `tl.add('.b', { x: 100 }, '-=0.2')`. Options: `delay`, `repeat`, `repeatDelay`, `yoyo`, `speed`, `ease` (applied to the overall progress), `autoplay`, `defaults` and the callbacks (`onStart`, `onUpdate`, `onComplete`, `onRepeat`, `onReverseComplete`). `onUpdate` fires once per frame while the playhead moves (playing or seeking), after that frame's DOM writes. Sequential tweens of the same property chain their start values.

Children: `add(targets, props, options?, position?)` (alias `to`), `from(targets, fromProps, options?, position?)`, `fromTo(targets, fromProps, toProps, options?, position?)`, `set(targets, props, position?)`, `call(fn, position?)`, `label(name, position?)`, and `add(animationOrTimeline, position?)` to nest. `tl.labels` is a `Map` of label → seconds.

---

## Physics

```ts
const s = spring(el, { x: 200, y: 50 }, { stiffness: 200, damping: 20 });   // or { bounce: .3, duration: .5 }
spring(el, { x: 0 });               // retarget: position and velocity are preserved
s.velocity;                          // { x: …, y: … } in units/s
await s;                             // resolves at rest

inertia(card, { x: { velocity: vx, min: 0, max: 600, snap: 100 } }, { power: 0.8, timeConstant: 0.35 });
```

`spring(targets, props, options?)`: props are end values (numbers or strings with units, colours too). Options: `stiffness` (default 100), `damping` (10), `mass` (1), or the perceptual pair `bounce` (0–1) + `duration` (seconds); `velocity` (units/s, a number or per-property map), `restDelta`, `restSpeed`, `onUpdate`, `onComplete`. Calling `spring()` again on a moving property retargets it (position and velocity kept); the latest call's `onUpdate` replaces the earlier one for that property, and every distinct `onComplete` fires once at rest, so a follower can pass a fresh options literal on every event. There is no `delay` or `ease`: call it later, or use `animate()` with `ease: 'spring(…)'` for a timed spring. `inertia()` adds `power` (0.8), `timeConstant` (0.35 s), `bounceStiffness` and `bounceDamping`; each prop is `{ velocity, min?, max?, snap? }` or a bare velocity. All three return a `PhysicsAnimation`.

---

## Scroll & viewport

```ts
const stop = scroll(animate('.bar', { scaleX: [0, 1] }, { ease: 'linear' }));       // page progress
scroll(animate(img, { y: [-80, 80] }), { target: img, offset: ['start end', 'end start'], smooth: 0.1 });
scroll((p) => (counter.textContent = Math.round(p * 100) + '%'), { container: panel });
inView('.reveal', (el) => { animate(el, { opacity: [0, 1] }); return () => animate(el, { opacity: 0 }); }, { amount: 0.3 });
scroll(compositor('.hero', { scale: [1, 1.15], opacity: [1, 0] }, { ease: 'linear' }), { target: hero, offset: ['start start', 'end start'] });
```

Give `scroll()` a `compositor()` animation and it's attached to a native `ScrollTimeline` where the browser has one: the browser scrubs it in step with the scroll, and no JavaScript runs while scrolling. The `offset` range is measured from layout (and again on resize), so it means the same as on the JavaScript path. Without `ScrollTimeline`, or with `smooth`, it's scrubbed from the scroll event instead (`native: false` forces that). All `scroll()` links on one scroller share one passive listener that reads the scroll position once per event; a link driving an animation only seeks when its progress changes, while a function subject is called on every event.

`compositor()` animations honour `engine.reducedMotion` (they jump to the end), and `revert()` cancels them and puts back the inline styles from before.

---

## SVG

`morph(a, b) → (t) => d`, `morphPlan(a, b)`, `morphSequence([a, b, c]) → { template, frames }` (one shared template for N shapes), `pathData(src)` (path data of a string, element or selector), `pathLength(p)`, `pathBounds(p) → [minX, minY, maxX, maxY]`, `normalizePath(p)`, `shapeToPath(el)` and `new MotionPath(p).at(t) → { x, y, angle }`. Shape builders return path data: `circle(cx, cy, r)`, `ellipse(cx, cy, rx, ry?)`, `rect(x, y, w, h, rx?, ry?)`, `polygon(points, closed?)` and `star(cx, cy, points, outer, inner?, rotation?)`.

```ts
import { animate, morph, circle, star, MotionPath } from 'anikit';
animate('#blob', { d: star(50, 50, 5, 40, 18) }, { duration: 0.8, ease: 'inOutCubic' });  // morph a <path>
const at = morph(circle(50, 50, 40), star(50, 50, 6, 45, 20));   // at(0.5) → path data halfway
animate('#dot', { path: { path: '#track', rotate: true } }, { duration: 3, ease: 'linear' });
const { x, y, angle } = new MotionPath('#track').at(0.25);
animate('#line', { draw: [0, 1] }, { duration: 1.2 });            // stroke draws in
```

Path utilities (all return path data strings or numbers; a source is path data, an SVG element or a selector):

```ts
pathLength('M0,0 L100,0');                       // 100
pathBounds(circle(50, 50, 40));                  // [10, 10, 90, 90]
pathArea(rect(0, 0, 10, 20));                    // 200
pathData('#logo path');                          // the d of an element (shapes are converted)
shapeToPath(document.querySelector('circle')!);  // <circle>/<rect>/<ellipse>/<line>/<poly*> → path data
normalizePath('M0 0 H10 V10 Z');                 // absolute cubic segments: 'M0 0C3.333 0 …Z'
ellipse(50, 50, 40, 20); polygon([[0, 0], [10, 0], [5, 8]]);
trimPath('M0,0 L100,0', 0.25, 0.75);            // the middle half: 'M25 0C41.667 0 58.333 0 75 0'
transformPath('M0 0 L10 0', [2, 0, 0, 2, 5, 5]);   // apply a 2D matrix [a, b, c, d, e, f]
pathThrough([[0, 0], [50, 40], [100, 0]], { curviness: 1 });   // smooth curve through points
simplifyPath(d, 1);                              // fewer points within 1 unit
flattenPath('M0,0 L10,0 L10,10');                // [[[0, 0], [10, 0], [10, 10]]] polylines per subpath
const plan = morphPlan(circle(0, 0, 10), rect(0, 0, 10, 10));      // { template, from, to }
const seq = morphSequence([circle(0, 0, 10), rect(0, 0, 10, 10), star(0, 0, 5, 10)]);   // { template, frames }
```

---

## Text, layout, compositor, batches

```ts
const { chars, words, lines, revert } = splitText('h1', { type: 'lines,words,chars' });
animate(chars, { y: ['100%', 0], opacity: [0, 1] }, { delay: stagger(0.02) });

// Lines rising from behind a mask; re-split (and the animation handed over) when the width changes
splitText('.lede', { type: 'lines', mask: 'lines', autoSplit: true,
  onSplit: ({ lines }) => animate(lines, { yPercent: [100, 0] }, { delay: stagger(0.08), ease: 'outCubic' }) });

flip('.item', () => grid.classList.toggle('dense'), { duration: 0.6, ease: 'spring(bounce: .2)' }); // see "Layout transitions"

compositor('.toast', { y: [20, 0], opacity: [0, 1] }, { ease: 'spring(bounce: .4)' }); // compositor thread

const b = batch(50_000, { x: (i) => [0, i % 500], y: [0, 300], a: [0, 1] },
                { duration: 2, delay: stagger(0.00005), onUpdate: () => draw(b.data, b.stride) });
// b.data: Float32Array (count * stride), e.g. gl.bufferSubData(gl.ARRAY_BUFFER, 0, b.data)
```

- `splitText(targets, { type: 'chars' | 'words' | 'lines' (comma separated, default 'words,chars'), charClass, wordClass, lineClass, mask, maskClass, autoSplit, onSplit }) → { chars, words, lines, masks, split(), revert() }`. Characters are grapheme-safe (emoji stay whole). Line wrappers are direct children of the element; inline markup that spans lines (`<b>`, `<a>`) is continued on the next line by a copy without its `id`. Runs against the paragraph's direction (a Hebrew phrase in English text) are wrapped in `<span dir unicode-bidi:isolate>` so they keep their order, and Arabic, Syriac and N'Ko character pieces carry zero-width joiners so letters keep their joined forms.
- `splitText` options: `mask: 'lines' | 'words' | 'chars'` wraps each unit in an `overflow: clip` element (returned in `masks`; class via `maskClass`). `autoSplit: true` splits again when an element's width changes and once web fonts have loaded, so lines match the layout. `onSplit(result)` runs after every split; return the animation that uses the pieces, and on a re-split it's reverted and the new one is moved to the same time. `result.split()` re-splits on demand, and `revert()` restores the markup (a `context()` does this too).
- `flip(targets, mutate, options?)` measures, runs `mutate()` (your DOM/class change), then animates from the old layout; see [Layout transitions](#layout-transitions-flip) for enter/leave, shared elements and presence.
- `compositor(targets, props, options?)` runs on the browser's compositor thread (Web Animations) with anikit easings, springs included; keeps going when the main thread is busy.
- `batch(count, props, options?) → Batch`: `data` (Float32Array, `count * stride`), `stride`, `channels` (`{ x: 0, y: 1, … }`), `get(i, prop)`. A prop is a shared keyframe list or `(index, count) => keyframes`.


---

## Marquees: `marquee`

An endless row (or column) of items — logos, tickers, testimonials — with no seam: the children move into a track, are cloned (`aria-hidden`, ids removed) until they cover the container twice, and the track moves and wraps every frame.

```ts
import { marquee, Marquee } from 'anikit';

const m: Marquee = marquee('.logos', { speed: 60, pauseOnHover: true, scrollBoost: 0.5 });
m.speed = -120;     // reverse and speed up (eases over `smoothing`, default 0.4 s)
m.pause();          // eases to a stop; m.play() resumes
m.revert();         // removes the clones and the track, restores the container
```

Options: `speed` (px/s, default 80; negative reverses), `axis` (`'x'` or `'y'`), `gap` (px; or set CSS `gap` on the container), `pauseOnHover`, `hoverSpeed` (multiplier while hovered), `scrollBoost` (speeds up and follows the page's scroll direction), `smoothing`. It re-measures on resize (`m.measure()` after changing the content), stands still under reduced motion, and is cleaned up by `context().revert()`. The `Marquee` controller exposes `offset` and the eased `velocity`.

## Magnetic and parallax: `magnetic`, `parallax`

```ts
import { magnetic, parallax, PointerFx } from 'anikit';

magnetic('.cta', { strength: 0.35, radius: 120, spring: { stiffness: 300, damping: 18 } });
const bg: PointerFx = parallax('.hero-bg', { speed: -0.4 });     // lags behind the page
parallax('.hero-fg', { speed: 0.2, smooth: 0.15 });              // runs slightly ahead
bg.revert();
```

- `magnetic(targets, { strength, radius, spring })`: elements lean towards the pointer (`strength` × its offset from their centre) once it is within `radius` px of their edge, and spring back when it leaves. Uses `x`/`y`, so it composes with other transforms.
- `parallax(targets, { speed, axis, smooth })`: a scroll-linked drift while each element crosses the viewport; `speed` is relative to the page (−0.5 lags, 0.5 leads). Built on `scroll()`, so it scrubs both ways.
- Both return a `PointerFx` (`revert()`, `kill()`), are cleaned up by `context().revert()`, and do nothing under reduced motion.

## Layout transitions: `flip`

`flip(targets, mutate, options?)` records where elements are, runs `mutate`, and animates every element from its old box to its new one using only transforms. It returns a `Timeline` holding every animation it started, so `await flip(...)` waits for all of them.

```ts
flip('.item', () => grid.classList.toggle('dense'), { duration: 0.6, ease: 'spring(bounce: .2)' });
flip('.card', () => applyFilter(), { fade: true });                    // removed cards fade out in place, new ones fade in
flip('.card', () => list.prepend(card), { enter: { scale: [0.6, 1], opacity: [0, 1] }, leave: { scale: 0.6, opacity: 0 } });
flip('[data-flip-id]', () => { thumb.hidden = true; modal.hidden = false; });  // shared element: modal grows out of the thumbnail
const state = flip.capture('.item'); reorder(); flip.from(state, { duration: 0.4 }); // manual capture
```

- **Re-queried targets:** when `targets` is a selector it's queried again after `mutate`, so elements added by the change are found. Pass `targets` in the options to name them explicitly.
- **Entering elements** (new, or hidden before) play `enter` keyframes, or `{ opacity: [0, 1] }` with `fade: true`, or whatever `onEnter(els)` returns.
- **Leaving elements** (removed from the DOM or hidden by the change) are put back at their last box with `position: absolute`, so their siblings reflow straight away. They play `leave` (or a fade, or `onLeave(els)`) and are then removed or hidden for real, with their inline styles restored. If a later change brings one back mid-exit, the exit is cancelled and it animates from where it is.
- **Shared elements:** two different elements with the same `data-flip-id` (or the same `id(el)`) are treated as one: the incoming one starts on the outgoing one's box. If both stay visible they cross-fade (`crossfade: false` to turn it off).
- **Interrupted flips** start from where the elements are on screen and end on their own transforms.
- **Nested and scrolled:** an element inside another moving element starts at its old box on screen, at any depth and with scaling. A `flip.capture()` followed by a page scroll and then `flip.from()` starts the elements where they were on the page (fixed-position elements where they were on screen).
